input.command:
gh pr create --title "perf(graph,vcs): bound git revwalk, cache tag globs, fix inference pathspecs" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
- Bound `commits_since_with_pathspec`'s revwalk to `since..HEAD` using gix's `with_hidden` frontier algorithm instead of two full unbounded walks — measured ~265x speedup (105.2ms → 0.397ms avg at 3000 commits), preserves the existing branchy-history correctness invariant.
- Cache compiled tag-template glob matchers across packages in `TagIndex::build`, avoiding redundant recompile+rescan when multiple packages share a `[[package-set]]` template.
- Fix commit-inference pathspecs to scope to the package's source directory instead of its manifest file path, so the `inference` feature actually matches real source changes.

Each finding is its own commit with a dedicated regression test confirmed failing before the fix, and passed an independent read-only review agent. Full detail (including measured before/after numbers) in `.claude/plans/ACTIVE.md`'s Track 7 entry.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo nextest run -p callisto-vcs -p callisto-graph` — 559/559 passed
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` / `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] Two independent review agents (explicitly read-only) passed all three findings, including a deep branchy-history correctness trace on the revwalk change
- [ ] Full-workspace `just ci` not run this session — see note below

**Note**: a pre-existing, unrelated environment issue was found and diagnosed during this work (`cargo nextest` + global `commit.gpgsign=true` causes ~120s hangs across ~66 git-fixture test call sites in 16 files, root-caused and reproduced on a clean checkout independent of this branch). It's documented in `ACTIVE.md` and deferred to its own track rather than folded into this PR's scope.

https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED
EOF
)"

A prior session diagnosed a real bug: `cargo nextest` spawns each test binary with no controlling TTY. On a developer machine with `git config --global commit.gpgsign true` set, any test that creates a real on-disk git repo and calls `git commit` without locally disabling signing triggers a real GPG signing attempt that `pinentry` can't service (no TTY to prompt on) — the test hangs ~120-140s waiting on a gpg-agent/pinentry timeout, or fails outright with "gpg: signing failed: No pinentry". This affects ~66 `git commit` call sites across 16 files in the workspace's test suite. There's a shared, canonical fixture helper — `callisto-fixtures::git::init_repo` — used by 2 of those files; the other ~14 independently duplicate their own version.

## The fix (this review's scope — only `crates/callisto-fixtures/src/git.rs`)

`init_repo` now runs 5 `git` commands instead of 3:
```rust
pub fn init_repo(root: &Path) {
    run_git(root, &["init", "-q", "-b", "main"]);
    run_git(root, &["config", "user.email", "test@example.com"]);
    run_git(root, &["config", "user.name", "Test"]);
    run_git(root, &["config", "commit.gpgsign", "false"]);
    run_git(root, &["config", "tag.gpgsign", "false"]);
}
```

git add crates/callisto-fixtures/src/git.rs
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(fixtures): make init_repo hermetic against ambient git config

Diagnosed this session: cargo nextest spawns each test binary with no
controlling TTY. On a machine with commit.gpgsign=true set globally,
any test creating a real repo via this shared helper would trigger a
real GPG signing attempt on commit -- pinentry can't prompt without a
TTY, so the test hangs ~120-140s on a gpg-agent timeout, or fails
outright with "gpg: signing failed: No pinentry". init_repo now sets
commit.gpgsign=false/tag.gpgsign=false in the repo's local config
(never touching the developer's real ~/.gitconfig), which git respects
as taking precedence over any global config. Also pins the initial
branch name (-b main), since init.defaultBranch is similarly ambient.

Regression test writes a throwaway GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL override (not the
real global config) forcing commit.gpgsign=true and an unusable
gpg.program, then asserts a commit still succeeds -- confirmed failing
before this fix, confirmed passing after. Fast and deterministic (the
poisoned gpg.program path doesn't exist, so a poisoned commit fails
immediately via "cannot exec" rather than actually hanging).

This is the canonical fixture helper (callisto-fixtures::git::init_repo);
~14 other independently-duplicated init_repo/run_git helpers across the
workspace still need the same fix -- follow-up commits, not covered here.
EOF
)"

Reference the canonical fix commit `a4eb5f0` plus your new commits. Commit that as its own final `docs:` commit.
8. Do NOT push or open a PR — leave that for the coordinating session.

Report back: which files you actually touched vs skipped (and why, if any), all commit SHAs, and confirmation that `cargo test --workspace` (or per-crate equivalents if workspace-wide is too slow given known nextest slowness elsewhere) is green for every crate you touched.

+Lighter TDD loop tier (no formal spec/plan, one crate per commit). Fixes a real bug surfaced during
+Track 7 (`track-7-revwalk-bounding`, PR #13, not yet merged when this track was cut): `cargo nextest`
+spawns each test binary with no controlling TTY, and on a developer machine with
+`commit.gpgsign=true`/`tag.gpgsign=true` set globally, any test that creates a real on-disk git repo
+and calls `git commit`/`git tag` without locally disabling signing triggers a real GPG signing attempt
+that `pinentry` can't service (no TTY to prompt on) — the test hangs ~120-140s waiting on a
+gpg-agent/pinentry timeout, or fails outright with "gpg: signing failed: No pinentry". Diagnosed via
+direct reproduction (confirmed NOT gpg-agent lock contention: 8 fully concurrent `git commit`s outside
+nextest completed in ~1s; confirmed the specific `cargo test` vs `cargo nextest` TTY distinction is the
+actual trigger) — see `feedback_diagnose_dont_guess_environment_issues.md` in the memory index for the
+process this followed. Two audit agents mapped the full scope: ~66 real `git commit` call sites across
+16 files build real git fixture repos without a local `commit.gpgsign=false` guard; a canonical shared
+helper existed (`callisto-fixtures::git::init_repo`) but only 2 of ~14 independently-duplicated
+`init_repo`/`run_git`-style helpers actually used it; a parallel audit confirmed no equivalent gap
+exists for npm/pip/cargo/twine/maturin shell-outs (all go through a mockable `CommandRunner` trait in
+both production and test code).
+
+**Fix**: `callisto-fixtures::git::init_repo` (the canonical helper) now sets `commit.gpgsign=false`/
+`tag.gpgsign=false` via local `git config` calls (never touching the developer's real `~/.gitconfig`,
+which git respects as taking lower precedence than local config) and pins `-b main` on `git init`
+(`init.defaultBranch` is a related ambient-config gap). A regression test
+(`crates/callisto-fixtures/src/git.rs`) proves this hermetically and fast: it writes a throwaway
+`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`-pointed poisoned config file (not the real global config) forcing
+`commit.gpgsign=true` and an unusable `gpg.program`, then asserts a commit still succeeds — confirmed
+failing before the fix, passing after, and independently re-verified by the reviewing agent via its own
+standalone experiment (0.05s run time, no hang, since the poisoned `gpg.program` path doesn't exist so
+a poisoned attempt fails immediately via "cannot exec" rather than actually invoking pinentry).
+
+Every other independently-duplicated helper across the workspace got the identical two-line fix
+(hand-patched in place, not migrated to import the shared helper — `callisto-fixtures` is
+AGPL-3.0-only, and per this project's layer-isolation invariant no new dev-dependency edges on it were
+introduced):

+  test's own inline init sequence (didn't call `init_repo` at all); `src/access.rs`'s `init_repo` fn.
+  Verified: `cargo nextest run -p callisto-vcs` — entire 38-test suite now completes in 0.345s (some of
+  these tests previously took 57-84s each under nextest).
+- **callisto-cli** (`f4a55cd7`): `tests/common/mod.rs`'s `setup_polyglot_git_repo`,
+  `tests/strict_flag_tests.rs`'s `make_git_workspace`, `tests/dry_run_invariant_tests.rs`'s `setup_repo`,
+  `src/commands/version.rs`'s `git_init_with_commit` (behind the `inference` feature). Verified:
+  `cargo nextest run -p callisto-cli --test strict_flag_tests --test dry_run_invariant_tests` — 20/20
+  pass in 1.003s total; `dry_run_invariant_tests` is the exact file that originally failed outright
+  with "No pinentry" in the session's first observed failure.
+- **callisto-graph** (`9fb0384e`): `src/commands/snapshot.rs`'s `git_init_with_commit`,
+  `src/commands/version.rs`'s `git_init_with_commit`, `tests/version_tests.rs`, `tests/snapshot_tests.rs`'s
+  `init_git_repo_with_commit`, `tests/publish_tests.rs`. `tests/tag_sha_fabrication_test.rs` already had
+  the correct fix (with its own explanatory comment) — left untouched; it's the file this fix pattern
+  was modeled on. Verified: `cargo nextest run -p callisto-graph --test snapshot_tests --test
+  version_tests --test publish_tests` — 38/38 pass in 0.541s total (previously ~60-84s each).
+- **callisto-moon** (`26d14b1b`): `tests/moon_wasm_sandbox.rs`'s async `run_git`-based init sequences
+  (two duplicate blocks). Verified via `cargo check`/`cargo clippy --features pdk` only (clean) — full
+  execution of this file's real wasmtime-backed sandbox test was not run given the prohibitive combined
+  build cost (native wasmtime/aws-lc-sys compile plus a from-scratch `wasm32-wasip1` build with no
+  cached artifact available); the change is mechanically identical to the four already-fully-verified
+  fixes above. Recommend confirming with a real `just wasm-check`/full test run in CI.

content.text: Confirmed root cause: `Path::new("Cargo.toml").starts_with(".")` is `false` in Rust — `package_paths`'s root-package sentinel `"."` (which real git's own pathspec engine understands as "match everything," and which correctly worked in `package_paths`'s original consumer that shells out to real git) doesn't have that meaning to this codebase's own Rust-based `location_matches` matcher. My Track 7 finding-3 fix newly routes a `"."` pathspec into that matcher for any root-level package, which now matches **zero** commits — worse than the bug it fixed. My test only covered a nested package, missing this edge case. Switching to the Track 7 branch to fix it properly.

    let changed_path = Path::new(path_str.as_ref());
